newsitem.title: USA: Norfolk urges Conrail to reject CSX deal.
newsitem.headline: Norfolk urges Conrail to reject CSX deal.

text.p: Norfolk Southern Corp. said Sunday that it will not participate in any deal that delivers less than $110 a share in cash to shareholders of Conrail Inc., the object of a takeover battle between Norfolk Southern and CSX Corp.
Norfolk Southern said it is urging Conrail shareholders to reject CSX Corp.'s $8.5 billion stock and cash merger agreement with Conrail.
Norfolk, Va.-based Norfolk Southern said it is putting shares of Conrail that were submitted in its tender offer into a voting trust to remove risk to shareholders if regulators reject the deal.

Norfolk Southern made its request ahead of Conrail's shareholder meeting to approve the deal set for Dec. 23, 1996. At the meeting, shareholders will be asked to permit Richmond, Va.-based CSX to buy 40 percent of Conrail in a tender offer.
As of Nov. 21, Norfolk Southern said 1.4 million Conrail shares were tendered and the offer is set to expire Dec. 16.
Conrail, which was not immediately available for comment, has approximately 80 million shares outstanding. CSX has acquired 19.9 percent of Conrail's shares, the Philadelphia-based railroad has said.
